thread:
elaine: FYI customer ACME just opened an escalation — clicking request IDs in the Console trace view returns "No trace found" even though their app logs show spans were emitted. They see 500 spikes + increased tail latency.

vikram: Can you paste the exact request-id and a quick repro? Also: which region & model route?

elaine: Region: eu-west-1, route: /v1/generate (hosted), customer request-id: 2f7a9c4b. Repro steps: call API with X-Request-ID header and then click the id in Console -> trace view. We get the toast: "No trace found for request 2f7a9c4b".

sophie: Any trace-ingest errors in the trace-processor logs? Can you check traces.indexer.metrics, ingestion_lag and consumer lag on Kafka?

elaine: I pulled a small snippet from the gateway logs around that request: 
```
2026-04-09T13:02:11Z gateway INFO request_id=2f7a9c4b route=/v1/generate status=200 duration_ms=412
2026-04-09T13:02:11Z auth-proxy DEBUG dropped-headers: ["X-Request-ID"]
2026-04-09T13:02:11Z trace-emitter INFO queued span batch size=3 trace_id=8a1f... started
2026-04-09T13:02:12Z trace-processor WARN no-index-fields: request_id missing for trace 8a1f...
```

vikram: That "dropped-headers" line is a smoking gun. If the auth-proxy strips X-Request-ID before the emitter indexes request_id, Console won't find the trace by request-id. Was there a proxy change?

sophie: There was an auth-proxy rollout yesterday (2026-04-08) that tightened forwarded header allowlist. It probably removed x-request-id. deploy-bot: 


deploy-bot: rollout auth-proxy v2.4.11 -> v2.4.12 started by @sophie 2026-04-08T22:14:03Z (canary then all).

elaine: Customer reports missing spans in trace timeline too — UI shows only parent span, children not linked. Could be partial ingestion or sampler mismatch.

vikram: Quick checklist to confirm: 
- Check trace-processor consumer lag: `kafkactl consumer-group -g traces_processor -o json | jq .lag`
- Grep trace-processor logs for "no-index-fields" and "request_id missing`"
- Look at traces.indexer metrics: `sum by(status) (rate(traces_indexer_index_total[5m]))`
- Check tracer agent version in gateway pod: `kubectl -n gateway exec gateway-0 -- cat /app/AGENT_VERSION`

elaine: I ran the grep and saw ~120 occurrences of "request_id missing" in the last hour. consumer lag is low. traces_indexer shows steady success counts though some 4xx indexing errors spiked.

sophie: Two likely issues: 1) header not forwarded (so request_id not set on spans), 2) the indexer schema expects `request_id` and `trace_id` both, and if request_id absent we can't link UI click -> trace. Short-term mitigation: index on trace_id fallback and map request-id from gateway logs. Long-term: re-enable forwarding.

vikram: Workable immediate steps: 
1) Patch indexer to index trace_id even without request_id (hotfix) — Sophie can you open patch?
2) Add a console-level fallback where clicking request-id attempts a trace_id search by querying recent gateway logs (best-effort)
3) Roll back auth-proxy allowlist change to restore X-Request-ID forwarding and redeploy canary to confirm.

sophie: I'll prepare the hotfix PR to index trace_id when request_id missing. I'll also revert the allowlist change in the canary namespace and monitor. PR will reference runbook: RB-231.

elaine: For customer repro, please run this curl to reproduce and then check trace-processor logs: 
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "X-Request-ID: 2f7a9c4b" -d '{"prompt":"hello"}' https://api.eu-west-1.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

vikram: Adding a quick command to query traces API by trace_id fallback: 
```
# search by trace_id (recent)
curl -s "https://tracing.internal/api/v1/traces?trace_id=8a1f..." | jq .
```

elaine: Noted — customer confirmed they can reproduce with curl and saw same missing-link UI. They've been given ETA two hours.

sophie: Patch PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/trace-indexer/pull/482 (hotfix to index trace_id fallback). Reverted allowlist in canary; canary requests show forwarded X-Request-ID now.

vikram: I'll prepare a postmortem template & assign follow-ups: 
- infra: audit all proxies for header forwarding (sophie)
- product/console: add trace_id fallback UX & log-linking (elaine)
- infra: add unit test to prevent allowlist regression (sophie)
- observability: add alert on `no-index-fields` > 50/hr (vikram)

elaine: Customer updated: after canary revert they now see traces linked correctly for new requests. Old requests that missed request_id remain unlinked — we're offering a manual mapping by providing trace_id from logs.

vikram: Closing loop: create incident ticket INC-2026-145 and mark P2. I'll add timeline + mitigation steps.

elaine: Thanks all. I'll keep the customer updated and drop the manual mapping steps into the ticket. :thumbsup:

sophie: Following up: hotfix merged and rolled to prod at 2026-04-09T15:07:12Z. Will schedule the allowlist test in CI.

deploy-bot: completed rollout auth-proxy v2.4.12 -> v2.4.12 (reverted change) by @sophie at 2026-04-09T15:06:58Z

elaine: Great, closing thread once INC-2026-145 is updated with links and customer confirmed.
